x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement: Ha Meem.
Some of them said: It is separate letters from the name of God, which is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and it is the Ha’ and the Meem from it.
Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwayh Al-Marwazi told me, he said: Ali bin Al-Hasan told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Alif, Lam, Ra, Nun, and Harun Al-Rahman are separate.

x: Others said: It is an oath sworn by God, and it is one of the names of God.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ha Meem is an oath that God swore, and it is one of the names of God.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: Ha Meem is one of the letters of the names of God.

x: Others said: Rather, it is one of the names of the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Ha Meem he said:
m: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.

x: Others said: It is an alphabet.

Others said: Rather, it is a name, and they supported their statement with the words of Shureih bin Awfa Al-Absi: It reminds me of Hamim and the spear is burning, so why don't you recite Hamim before advancing? Al-Kumait says: We found for you in Al-Ha-Mim a verse that was interpreted by a pious and knowledgeable person among us.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Muammar ibn al-Muthanna that he said:
m: Yunus, meaning al-Jarmi, said: Whoever says this statement is being rejected, because the surah Ha Meem has silent letters, so it was pronounced in the way it is spelled, and these are the names of surahs that were pronounced with vowels, and if a surah is named with one of these jazm letters, then it is inflected with i’rab. The statement about this, in my opinion, is similar to the statement about its sisters, and we have already explained that in His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem. So that is sufficient without repeating it in this place, if the statement about Ha-Mim and everything that came in the Qur’an in this manner, I mean the letters of the spelling, is one statement.

x: His statement:
h
The revelation of the Book is from God

, the Almighty, the All-Knowing. God Almighty says: From God, the Almighty, in His vengeance against His enemies, the All-Knowing of what they do of deeds and other things, the revelation of this Book. So the revelation is lifted by His statement: from God.
And regarding His statement:
h
Forgiver of sin there are two interpretations

: One of them is that it means He forgives the sins of His servants. If this meaning is intended, then Ghafir and Qaabil are lowered in two ways. One of them is from the intention of repeating from, so the meaning of the statement then is: The revelation of the Book from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing, from Ghafir of sin and Qaabil of repentance, because Ghafir of sin is an indefinite noun, and it is not more eloquent for it to be an adjective for a definite noun, which is an indefinite noun. The other is that its i'rab, which is an indefinite noun, is based on the i'rab of the first, as an adjective for it, because it occurs between it and His statement: Of length, which is a definite noun. It is also permissible for its i'rab, which is an indefinite noun, to follow the i'rab of the first, if it is praise.

i: And praise sometimes follows its i'rab of what precedes it, and sometimes it is changed from the i'rab of the first by the accusative or nominative, as the poet said:
x: Do not separate my people who are deaf to enmity and the scourge of the islands Those who descend into every arena and are good at the ties of kinship And as He, the Most High, said: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, * Possessor of the Glorious Throne, * Doer of whatever He intends.

(al-Buruj 85:14-16) So He raised Fa’al, which is a pure indefinite noun, and followed the definite article of Ghawwad Al-Wadud. The other is that its meaning is that this is from His attribute, the Most High, if He has always been Forgiving of the sins of His servants before the revelation of this verse and during its revelation, and after that, then it would be a correct definite noun and a correct adjective. He said, Forgiver of sin, and did not say sins, because what was meant by it was the action.

i: , then repentance can be the plural of repentance, just as the word dawmah is plural for dawmah, and the word awm is plural for awman, from the word awm of a ship, as the poet said:
x: He sailed the ship, but when it stopped them It may be a source of repentance.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: A man came to Umar and said: I have been killed, so is there any repentance for me? He said: Yes, work hard and do not despair. Then he recited: “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. Forgiver of sin
h
and Accepter of repentance

.” And His statement: Severe in punishment means that the Most High says: His punishment is severe for those He punishes who disobey Him. So do not rely on the breadth of His mercy, but be on your guard against Him by avoiding His transgressions and performing His obligations. Just as He does not make the criminals and wrongdoers despair of His forgiveness and acceptance of the repentance of those who repent from their crime, likewise He does not make them feel safe from His punishment and vengeance against them for what they have made permissible of what He has forbidden and committed of His transgressions. His saying: The One with bounty means: The One with grace and blessings extended to whomever He wills of His creation. It is said from this: So-and-so is bountiful to his companions if he has grace over them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
The Possessor of bounty
means: The Possessor of spaciousness and wealth.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Possessor of bounty meaning wealth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The One with the length means the One with the blessings.

x: Some of them said: Length means power.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Possessor of length

, he said: Length is power, that is length. And His statement: There is no god but Him, to Him is the final destination. He says: There is no deity worthy of worship except God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing,

x: God Almighty says: No one disputes God’s arguments and evidence for His Oneness by denying them, except those who have denied His Oneness. And His statement:
h
So let not their moving about in the lands deceive you

, God Almighty says: O Muhammad, do not be deceived by their moving about in the lands and their remaining and dwelling therein, despite their disbelief in their Lord, so that you think that they were only given respite and moved about, so they moved about in the lands despite their disbelief in God, and were not hastened with punishment and torment for their disbelief because they were on some of the truth. We did not give them respite for that, but rather that the Book might reach its term and that the word of torment, the torment of your Lord, might come to pass upon them.

c: Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So let not their moving about in the lands deceive you

- their travels therein, and their coming and going. Then he related to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the stories of the nations who denied their messengers, and informed him that they were in their arguments with His messengers in the same way as his people to whom He had sent the messengers, and that He would bring down upon them His vengeance when they reached their appointed time after His messengers had excused them and warned them of His punishment, as He had mentioned in His Book, thus informing His Prophet that His way with his people who followed the path of those people in denying and arguing with Him was His way of bringing down His vengeance upon them and His power over them. So God, the Exalted, said: “Before your people, who denied Your message to them, denied a Messenger who argued with you falsely, the people of Noah and the parties after them, and they are the nations who formed parties and gathered against their messengers by denying them, like Aad and Thamud, the people of Lot, the people of Madyan and their likes.”

x: And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The people of Noah denied before them
, and the parties after them, he said: the disbelievers. And His statement:
h
And every nation plotted against their Messenger to seize him

, God Almighty says: And every nation of these nations that denied their Messengers and were divided against their Prophets plotted against their Messenger who was sent to them to seize him and kill him.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And every nation plotted against their Messenger to seize him

: meaning to kill him. It was also said: with their Messenger, and it was also said: every nation, so the ha’ and the mim were directed to the man and not to the word nation. It was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: with its Messenger, meaning with the Messenger of the nation. And His statement:
h
And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth

, meaning: And they argued with their Messenger with falsehood in order to invalidate, through their argument with him and their dispute with him, the truth that he brought to them from God, of entering into His obedience, acknowledging His Oneness, and disavowing the worship of anything other than Him, just as the infidels of your people argue with you, O Muhammad, with falsehood. And His statement:
h
So I seized them

, so how was My punishment? God Almighty says: So I seized those who intended to seize their Messenger with punishment from Me, so how was My punishment for them? Did I not destroy them and make them an example for mankind, and a warning for those after them, and make their homes and dwellings empty of them, and a resting place for wild beasts?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So I seized them
, and how severe was My punishment. He said: Severe, by God.

evidence.text: It was mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah: with its Messenger, meaning with the Messenger of the nation.

x: God Almighty says: And just as My punishment was inflicted upon the nations who denied their messengers, whose stories I have related to you, O Muhammad, and My chastisement descended upon them because of their denial of their messengers and their argument with them falsely, in order to refute the truth, so too the word of your Lord was inflicted upon those among your people who disbelieved in God, who argue about the verses of God. His statement: that they are the companions of the Fire. The Arab scholars differed regarding the position of his statement that they are.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of that is: The word of your Lord has come true upon those who disbelieved that they are the companions of the Fire: that is, because they are, or because they are not in the place of the object of there is no, like your saying: I have established that they are. If that were the case, it would also have come true because they are.

Others said: that they are is a substitute for the word, as if the word had truly established that they are the companions of the Fire. The correct thing to say about this is that his saying they is a translation of the word, meaning: And the punishment of the Fire, which God promised to the unbelievers, is due to them.

God Almighty says: Those who carry the Throne of God from among His angels, and from those around His Throne, from among the angels who surround it, glorify the praises of their Lord meaning: they pray to their Lord with His praise and thanks and believe in Him meaning: they acknowledge God that they have no god but Him, and they bear witness to that, they are not too proud to worship Him and they ask forgiveness for those who believe meaning: they ask their Lord to forgive the sins of those who have acknowledged the same as they acknowledged the Oneness of God and the disavowal of every deity other than Him, so He pardons them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And they ask forgiveness for those who believe for the people of There is no god but God
. And His statement: Our Lord,
h
You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge
. There is an omission in this statement, which is they say. The meaning of the statement is: And they seek forgiveness for those who have believed, saying: Our Lord,
h
You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge
. What is meant by His statement:
h
You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge

is: Your mercy and knowledge have encompassed all of Your creation, so You know everything, and nothing is hidden from You. You have had mercy on Your creation and encompassed them with Your mercy. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative of mercy and knowledge.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The accusative of that is like the accusative of you like him, a slave, because you made mercy and knowledge an object for everything, and it is an object for it, and the subject is the ta’, and mercy and knowledge came as an explanation, and you occupied them with the verb as you occupied the example with the ha’, so that is why you placed it in the accusative likening it to the object after the subject.

Another said: It is from the transferred, and it is an explanation, and his mercy and knowledge encompassed, and he encompassed everything with mercy, as you say: my soul was pleased with him, and my soul was pleased with him. And he said: Do you have someone like him, a slave? For quantities can only be known, like I have a pound of oil, and the example is unknown, but its wording is the wording of the definite and the slave is indefinite, so that is why he placed the slave in the accusative, and it can be raised.

i: And he cited as evidence for his saying that the saying of the poet: There is no one like you, Ma'ad and all the tribes of Qahtan, who is counted He said:
x: The singular is rejected because it is indefinite.
He said: If I said: There is no man like you, and a man like you, and a man like you, it is permissible, because like is indefinite, even if its wording is definite. And His statement:
h
So forgive those who repent and follow Your way
, meaning: So pardon the crime of those of Your servants who repented from associating partners with You, and returned to Your monotheism, and followed Your commands and prohibitions.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So forgive those who repent from polytheism. His saying:
h
And follow your path

, meaning: And they took the path that you commanded them to take, and they adhered to the method that you commanded them to adhere to, and that is entering into Islam. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And follow your way: meaning obey you. His statement: And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire means: And avert from those who repented from polytheism and followed Your path the punishment of Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection.

x: God Almighty says, informing us about the supplication of His angels for His servants who have faith in Him, saying: Our Lord,
h
and admit them

to the Gardens of Eden meaning: the gardens of residence which You have promised them meaning: which You have promised to the people of repentance to Your obedience if You admit them into it and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring meaning: And admit with these those who repented and followed Your way to the Gardens of Eden whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring, and did the righteous deeds that please You in this world. And He mentioned that a man’s parents, his children, and his wife will enter Paradise with him, even if they did not do what he did, by the grace of God’s mercy upon him.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Yaman Al-Ajli narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, who said:
m: A man will enter Paradise and say: Where is my father, where is my mother, that is, my son, that is, my wife? It will be said: They did not do as you did. He will say: I used to work for myself and for them. It will be said: Admit them to Paradise. Then he recited: Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. So, since that is its meaning, it is in the accusative case in apposition to the ha’ and the mim in His statement:
h
And admit them

. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case in apposition to the ha’ and the mim in I promised them. “Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” He says: Indeed, You, O our Lord, are the Exalted in taking revenge on Your enemies, the Wise in managing Your creation.

x: He, the Most High, means by His statement, informing us of what His angels said: Protect them: Turn away from them the evil consequences of their bad deeds that they committed before their repentance and return to God. They say: Do not hold them accountable for that, so do not punish them for it. “And whoever You turn away evil deeds on that Day - You have had mercy on him.” He says: And whoever You turn away the evil consequences of his bad deeds because of that on the Day of Resurrection - You have had mercy on him and saved him from Your punishment. “And that is the great attainment,” because whoever is saved from the Fire and enters Paradise has succeeded, and that is undoubtedly the great attainment. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of bad deeds, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And protect them from evil deeds: meaning torment.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muammar ibn Bashir told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mutraf, who said:
m: We found that the most sincere servants of God to other servants are the angels, and the most deceitful servants of God to other servants are the devils. And he recited, Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [God] with praise of their Lord
r
(Ghafir 40:7)
... the verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Mutraf said:
m: We found that the most deceitful of God’s servants to God’s servants are the devils, and we found that the most sincere of God’s servants to God’s servants are the angels.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieved in God will be called out in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection when they enter it. They will hate themselves for entering it when they see the types of torment that God has prepared for them in it. It will be said to them: God’s hatred of you, O people, in this world, when you were called therein to believe in God and you disbelieved, is greater than your hatred of yourselves today because of the wrath that has befallen you of God. And in the same way that we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
The hatred of God is greater
, he said: They hated themselves when they saw their deeds, and God’s hatred of them in this world when they were called to faith, but they disbelieved, is greater.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out, ‘
h
The hatred of God is greater

than your hatred of yourselves when you were invited to faith and you disbelieved.’ He says: The hatred of God for the people of misguidance when faith was offered to them in this world, but they abandoned it and refused to accept, is greater than the hatred they felt for themselves when they witnessed God’s punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out, ‘
h
The hatred of God is greater
than your hatred of yourselves’ in the Fire, when you were called to faith in this world, but you disbelieved.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: They will be called out, ‘Because of the hatred of God’… the verse, he said: When they entered the Fire, they hated themselves for the sins of God that they committed, so they were called out: God’s hatred for you when He called you to Islam is more intense than your hatred for yourselves today when you entered the Fire. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of this lam in His statement:
h
The hatred of God is greater

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra said: It is the lam of initiation, as if they are calling and it is said to them, because in calling there is a saying. He said: And similar to it in grammar is when it is said: Zaid is better than Amr.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning is: They are calling that God’s hatred of you, but the lam is sufficient to prevent you from saying in speech: I called that Zaid is standing. He said: And similar to it is His statement: Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time
r
(Yusuf 12:35)

. The lam is like an in every speech that follows a saying such as they call and they inform and the like. Another one of them said: This is the lam of the oath, it is used with the narration and what is similar to the narration, to indicate that what comes after it is a resumption. He said: It is not permissible in the responses of faith for it to take the place of the oath, because the lam was with it the nun or it was not, so it was sufficient for the oath, because it does not occur except with it. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: She entered to call to prayer, and that what follows it is a resumption and that it is the lam of the oath.
And His saying: Our Lord,
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice
we have already mentioned this in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it in this place, but we will mention some of what some of them said about it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice

, he said: They were dead in the loins of their fathers, then God gave them life in this world, then caused them to die the inevitable death, then He gave them life for the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, so they are two lives and two deaths. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say:

c: Ubaid told us:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice
, that it is the statement of God:
h
How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead
and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, and then to Him you will be returned. (al-Baqarah 2:28) Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said:

c: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice
. He said: It is like His statement:
h
How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead
? (al-Baqarah 2:28)... the verse.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice
, he said: It is like the one in Surat al-Baqarah 2:And you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life (al-Baqarah 2:28).

c: Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding this verse, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice, he said: You created us when you were nothing, then You caused us to die, then You gave us life.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisn, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You caused us to die twice and brought us to life twice
, they said: They were dead and God brought them to life, then caused them to die, then brought them to life.

x: Others said about it what:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his statement:
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice

, he said: They were killed in this world, then they were brought to life in their graves, so they asked or gave sermons, then they were killed in their graves, then they were brought to life in the Hereafter.

x: Others said about that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Our Lord,
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice

, he said: He created them from the loins of Adam when He took the covenant from them, and he recited: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-A’raf 7:172), and he recited until he reached the falsifiers (al-A’raf 7:173). He said: So He made them forget the action and took the covenant from them. He said: And He extracted one of the shortest ribs of Adam and created Eve from it. It was mentioned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: And that is the statement of God: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women
r
(Al-Nisa’: 1)

. He said: After that, He dispersed from them in the wombs many creations. He recited: He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation (al-Zumar 39:6). He said: Creation after that. He said: So when He took the covenant from them, their mothers, then He created them. In the wombs, then their mothers, then He will revive them on the Day of Resurrection. This is the saying of God: Our Lord,
h
You caused us to die twice and You gave us life twice
, so we acknowledged our sins. And he recited the saying of God: And We took from them a solemn covenant.
r
(An-Nisa’: 154)

He said on that day and he recited the saying of God: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you with when you said, ‘We hear and we obey.’ (al-Ma’idah 5:7) His saying:
h
So we confessed our sins

means: So we acknowledged the sins we committed in this world. So is there a way out? He says: Is there a way out for us from the Fire, so that we may return to this world and do the good that we used to do in it?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Is there a way out? So is there a way out for the world?

x: And in this speech there is something omitted that is sufficient in the apparent meaning of its mention, which is: “So answer, there is no way to that. This is what you have of punishment, O disbelievers.” That if God alone is called upon, you disbelieve, so you deny that divinity is exclusively for Him, and you say, Have I made the gods one god? [p. 5]. And if a partner is associated with Him, you will believe. He says: And if a partner is attributed to God, the one who attributed that to him will believe. Then the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great. He says: So the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, over all things, the Great, to whom everything below Him is insignificant today.

God Almighty says: He who shows you, O people, His proofs and evidence of His Oneness and Lordship, and sends down to you provision from the sky, meaning He sends down to you from your provisions from the sky by the abundant rain with which He brings forth your sustenance from the earth, and the nourishment of your livestock for you. And none will remember except he who turns back, meaning none will remember God’s proofs which He made proof of His Oneness, and take heed from them and learn from them, and know the truth of what they indicate, except he who turns back. He says: except he who returns to His Oneness and turns to His obedience.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Except for he who repents, he said: He who turns to obeying God.

x: And His statement: So call upon God, making your religion sincere to Him means that the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him: So worship God, O believers, making your obedience sincere to Him, not associating anything with Him besides Him, even though the disbelievers dislike it meaning: Even though the disbelievers who associate idols and rivals with Him dislike your worship of Him, making your obedience sincere to Him.

God Almighty says: He is of high rank. He raised his statement: of high rank as a subject, and if it had come in the accusative case as a response to his statement: So call upon God, it would have been correct to say: Possessor of the Throne meaning: Possessor of the Throne who encompasses everything below it. His saying:
h
He sends the spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants
. He says: He sends down revelation by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of the spirit in this context.
Some of them said: It means revelation.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: He casts the spirit by His command, he said: The revelation by His command.

x: Others said: He meant the Qur’an and the Book.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Harun bin Idris Al-Asamm told me, he said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He sends the spirit of His command upon whomever He wills of His servants
, he said: He means by the spirit: the Book that He sends down upon whomever He wills.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
He sends the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants
, and he recited, And thus We have revealed to you a spirit by Our command
r
(Ash-Shura 42:52)

, he said: This Qur’an is the spirit. God revealed it to Gabriel, and Gabriel is a spirit that brought it down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He recited, The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (Ash-Shu’ara 62:193). He said: So the books that God sent down to His prophets are the spirit, to warn with them of what God said on the Day of Meeting, The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows
r
(An-Naba 78:38)
. He said: The spirit is the Qur’an. My father used to say it. Ibn Zayd said: They will stand for Him in rows between the heaven and the earth when He, the Majestic and Glorious, descends.

x: Others said: It means prophecy.
Those who said this: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
He sends the spirit of His command upon whomever He wills of His servants
, he said: Prophethood is upon whomever He wills. These statements are similar in meaning, even though the wording of their proponents differs regarding them. His statement,
h
To warn of the Day of Meeting

, means: To warn those of His servants upon whom He sends the Spirit, of the command of God to warn of His creation of the punishment of the Day when the people of Heaven and Earth will meet, which is the Day of Meeting, and that is the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: The Day of Meeting is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, the greatness of God and His warning to His servants.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: The Day of Meeting means the day on which the people of heaven and earth, and the Creator and creation, will meet.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: On the Day of Meeting the people of Heaven and the people of Earth will meet.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: The Day of Meeting he said: The Day of Resurrection. He said: The day when the servants will meet.

x: And His statement:
h
On the Day they will come forth
, nothing of them will be hidden from God means by His statement,
h
On the Day they will come forth

, the warned ones to whom God sent His messengers to warn them, and they will be visible, meaning to the onlookers, with no mountain or tree separating them from each other, and no barrier concealing them from each other, but they will be in a flat, smooth plain with no unevenness or crookedness. And <they>in His statement,
h
On the Day they will come forth

is in the nominative case with what follows it, like the saying of the one who says: I did that on the day of Al-Hajjaj, the emir. The Arabists differed about the reason why hum bi-yawm was not made genitive when it was added to it.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: yawm was added to hum in meaning, and therefore yawm is not given a tanween, as he said: The day they will be tested upon the Fire (al-Dhariyat 51:13) and he said: This is a day on which they will not speak (al-Mursalat 77:35). Its meaning is: This is the day of their trial, but since it began with the noun and was built upon it, it was not able to make it genitive, and the addition in meaning was to the trial. This only happens if the day is in the meaning of idh, otherwise it is ugly. Do you not see that you say: If only you were in the time of Zayd the emir? That is, when Zayd is the emir. If you had said: I will meet you in the time of Zayd the emir, it would not be good.

Another said: The meaning of that is that the times were made in the meaning of idh and idha, and therefore they remained in the accusative case in the nominative, genitive, and accusative cases. So he said: And from the disgrace of that day
r

, so they made it genitive, and the position is genitive, and that is evidence that it was made in the position of the tool. It is permissible to make it inflected in the ways of inflection, because it is apparent that the names appear. Don't you see that the pronoun does not return to it as it does to nouns? Rather, the pronoun returned with a nun and was declined and not added. So it was said: I liked the day in which you say, since it did not leave the meaning of the tool and the mention returned to it, it became a correct noun. He said: It is permissible in idh to say: I came to you when you stand, just as you say: I came to you on the day the judge sits, so it is a known time.

As for I came to you on the day you stand, there is no difficulty in it, and it is permissible from all of them. And he said: And this that is called a non-pure addition. The correct thing to say in this regard, in my opinion, is that the accusative case of day and all other times in such a position is similar to the accusative case of tools, as they occur in their positions. And if the faces of inflection are parsed, it is because they appear as nouns, so they are treated in the same way as them. And His saying: Nothing about them is hidden from God meaning, nor anything about the deeds they did in this world.
Qatada used to say about that what:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
On the Day they will come forth
, nothing of them will be hidden from God but they will come forth before Him on the Day of Resurrection, and they will not hide behind a mountain or a layer of mud. And his saying:
h
To whom belongs the dominion today
? He means by that: The Lord says:
h
To whom belongs the dominion today

. He left out mentioning say because the meaning of the speech is sufficient for it and his saying: To God, the One, the Prevailing. We have already mentioned the narration that came in that regard previously and the meaning of the speech: The Lord says:
h
To whom belongs the dominion today

? That is on the Day of Resurrection. He will answer himself and say: To God, the One, who has no equal or likeness, the Prevailing over everything other than Him by His power, the Victorious by His might.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what He will say on the Day of Resurrection when He will raise His creation from their graves for the Day of Judgment: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. He says: Today every worker will be rewarded for his work and will be given the reward for his work. The one who does good will be rewarded for good, and the one who does evil will be given his punishment. And His statement:
h
There will be no injustice today

means: No one will be deprived of the reward he deserved for his work in this world, so that it will be reduced if he was a good person, nor will a wrongdoer be burdened with the sin of a crime he did not commit, so that he will be punished for it. Indeed, God is swift in account means: God is swift in calling His servants to account on that day for the deeds they did in this world. He mentioned that that day will not be halfway through until the people of Paradise have taken their rest in Paradise and the people of Hell have taken their rest in Hell, and He has completed their reckoning and judgement between them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet: And warn, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people of the approaching Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, when they will meet God for their evil deeds, and they will deserve God’s painful punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, The approaching Day, he said: The Day of Resurrection.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And warn them of the approaching Day
means the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And warn them of the approaching Day
, he said: The Day of Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And warn them of the approaching Day
, he said: The Day of Resurrection, and he recited: “The approaching Day has drawn near. There is none to avert it but God” (al-Najm 53:57-58). And His statement:
h
When the hearts are at the throats

, stifling, God Almighty says: When the hearts of the servants, out of fear of God’s punishment, are at their throats, they have protruded from their chests, and they have stuck to their throats, stifling them. They try to return them to their places in their chests, but they do not return, nor do they exit their bodies, so they die. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
When the hearts are at the throats
, he said: The hearts have fallen into the throats out of fear, so they neither leave nor return to their places.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: h
When the hearts are at the throats

, stifling. He said: Their hearts were removed from their places and became stuck in their throats, so they did not leave their bodies so that they would die, and they did not return to their places so that they would settle. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative of Kāzimeen.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is accusative in the state of circumstance, as if he meant: since the hearts are at the throats in this state.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: The alif and lam are a substitute for the addition, as if he said: since their hearts are at their throats in the state of their suppression. Another of them said: It is accusative by cutting off the meaning that comes from mentioning them in the hearts and throats, meaning: since their hearts are at their throats, suppressing. He said: If you wish, you can cut it off from the ha’ in His statement and warn them. He said: The first is better in Arabic, and I have already explained the reason for that. And His statement:
h
The wrongdoers will have no protector or intercessor

. God Almighty says: On that Day, the disbelievers will have no protector or intercessor to protect them and ward off from them the great punishment of God that has befallen them, nor will they have an intercessor to intercede for them with their Lord, so that they will be obeyed in what they intercede for and answered in what they ask for.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: For the wrongdoers there is neither a friend nor an intercessor. He said: Who is concerned with their affair, nor is there an intercessor for them. His saying,
h
He is obeyed is a connection to the intercessor

. The meaning of the statement is: The wrongdoers have no intimate friend or intercessor. If someone intercedes, he will be obeyed in what he intercedes for, so his intercession will be answered and accepted.

x: And His statement,
h
He knows the treachery of the eyes

, says the Most High, informing about His own attributes: Your Lord knows what the eyes of His servants have betrayed, and what their breasts conceal, meaning: and what their hearts conceal. He says: Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, not even what his soul speaks to him and what his heart conceals when he looks, what he wants with his look and what he intends with his heart. And God judges with truth, meaning: God, the Most High, judges with truth concerning that which the eyes have betrayed in their gaze, and which the breasts have concealed from the sight of the eyes. He rewards those who closed their sight and diverted it from His prohibitions, fearing the standing before Him and being questioned about it, with goodness, and those who hesitated to look and whose hearts resolved to commit indecencies if they were able to, with their reward.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that: Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Marwazi told me, he said:

c: Ali bin Hussein bin Waqid told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
He knows the treachery of the eyes

if you look at her, intending to betray her or not. And what the hearts conceal if you are able to do so, whether you will commit adultery with her or not. He said: Then he was silent, then he said: Shall I not tell you about the one that follows it? I said: Yes. He said: And God judges with truth is able to reward good with good, and bad with bad. Indeed, it is God who is the Hearing, the Seeing. Al-Hasan said: So I said to Al-A’mash:

c: Al-Kalbi told me, except that he said:
m: God is able to reward bad with bad, and reward good with ten times. Al-A’mash said: What Al-Kalbi has with me is only insignificant.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
He knows the treachery of the eyes
, he said: The eyes looking at what God has forbidden.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: the traitor of the eyes means he knows his slander with his eye, and his closing his eyes to what God does not love or approve of.

x: And His statement:
h
And those they invoke besides Him do not judge at all

means: The idols and deities that these polytheists among your people worship besides Him do not judge at all, because they do not know anything and are not capable of anything. God Almighty says to them: So worship the One who has power over all things, and nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him. He rewards your good-doer for good and your evil-doer for evil, not that which has no power and knows nothing. He knows the good-doer from the evil-doer, so He rewards the good-doer and punishes the evil-doer. And His statement: Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing means: Indeed, God is the All-Hearing of what your tongues utter, O people, the All-Seeing of what you do, encompassing all of that and counting it against you, so that He may reward all of you accordingly on the Day of Judgment. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: And those whom they invoke besides Him. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as and those whom you invoke besides Him with a ta’ as a direct address. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a ba’ as a direct address. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: And those whom they invoke besides Him.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as and those whom you invoke besides Him with a ta’ as a direct address.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a ba’ as a direct address.

x: God Almighty says: Did not these people who persisted in their polytheism with God, who denied His Messenger from Quraysh, in the land, and see what was the end of those who were before them meaning: so that they might see what was the end of the nations who were before them from the nations who followed their path, in disbelief in God and denying His Messengers. They were stronger than them meaning: Those nations who were before them were stronger than them in power and left more traces on the earth, but their great strength and huge bodies did not benefit them when God’s command came to them and seized them for their crimes and transgressions, but He destroyed their gatherings and their dwellings became empty because of their wrongdoing. And they had no protector from God meaning: And they had no protector from God’s punishment when it came to them, to protect them or ward it off from them.

c: Like what Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they had no protector from God to protect them, nor to benefit them.

x: God Almighty says: This is what We did to those nations who came before, the polytheists of Quraysh, by destroying them for their sins. We did to them because the messengers of God came to them with clear proofs, meaning with signs indicating the truth of what they were calling them to of the Oneness of God and the conclusion of His obedience. But they disbelieved, meaning: they denied its message, rejected the Oneness of God, and refused to obey God. So God seized them, meaning: God seized them with His punishment and destroyed them. He is Powerful, Severe in Punishment, meaning: God is All-Powerful, Nothing can subdue Him, Nothing can overcome Him, and Nothing He wills is beyond His power. He is Severe in His punishment of whoever He punishes of His creation. This is a threat from the polytheists of Quraysh, who denied His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says to them: Beware, O people, of following their path in denying Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denying the Oneness of God, and disobeying His commands and prohibitions, or He will lead you to hasten your destruction. You have your own path.

God the Almighty says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for what he encountered from the polytheists of his people from Quraysh, by informing him of what Moses encountered from those to whom he was sent of denial, and informing him that he was exalted over them, and that he would make evil prevail over those who opposed and opposed him, as was His practice with Moses, peace be upon him, when He exalted him and destroyed his enemy Pharaoh. And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs meaning with His proofs. And a clear authority meaning a clear excuse, meaning: and His clear arguments for those who see them as a proof that confirms what Moses called for. To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, but they said, ‘A lying magician.’ Those to whom Moses was sent said to Moses: He is a magician who uses magic to enchant the staff, so that whoever looks at it sees it as a moving snake. Liar means: He lies about God and claims that He sent him as a messenger to the people.
To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, and they said, 'A lying magician.'

God Almighty says: When Moses came to those to whom God had sent him with the truth from Us, and that was his coming to them with the belief in the oneness of God and working in obedience to Him, while establishing proof against them, that God had sent him to them with the call to that, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believed’ in God ‘with him’ from among the Children of Israel ‘and keep their women alive’ meaning: and keep their women for service.

How was it said: But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive,’ Pharaoh killed the children of the Children of Israel out of fear of the newborn, who he had been told would lead to the loss of his kingdom and the destruction of his people. This was, as it is said, before God sent Moses as a prophet?

This command to kill the sons of those who believed with Moses and keep their women alive was an order from Pharaoh and his people after the first order that was from Pharaoh before the birth of Moses.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, ‘Kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive.’ He said: This is a killing other than the first killing that took place. And His statement,
h
And the plot of the disbelievers is only in error
, means: The plot of the disbelievers against the people of faith in God is nothing but injustice toward the path of truth, turning away from the intended path, and taking without guidance.

x: God Almighty says: And Pharaoh said to his al-Nas 114:Leave me to kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord whom he claims sent him to us to protect him from us I fear that he will change your religion meaning: I fear that he will change your religion that you are following with his magic. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: or that corruption should appear on earth. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Basra read it as and that corruption should appear on earth without an alif, and this is also the case in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Medina. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as or that with an alif, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an as appears on earth with a fatha on the ya’ and raising the corruption. The correct statement in this regard, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning.

This is because if corruption is made apparent, then it is apparent, and if it is apparent, then by making its appearance apparent, so in reading with one of the two readings there is clear evidence of the correctness of the meaning of the other. As for the reading of or that it appears with the alif and with its deletion, then they are also close in meaning. This is because if something is changed to its opposite, then there is no doubt that the opposite of what was changed to first is the apparent one, not what was changed. So whether he made his report about his fear of Moses changing their religion with the waw or with the waw, because changing their religion was, in his view, the appearance of corruption, and the appearance of corruption was, in his view, the change of religion. The interpretation of this statement is: I fear that Moses will change your religion, which you are following, or that he will establish in your land, the land of Egypt, the worship of his Lord, whom he calls you to worship.
And that, in his view, is corruption. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: I fear that your religion will be changed - meaning your current situation - or that corruption will appear on earth. Corruption, in his view, means working in obedience to God.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: or that corruption should appear on earth.

The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Basra read it as and that corruption should appear on earth without an alif, and this is also the case in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Medina.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as or that with an alif, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an as appears on earth with a fatha on the ya’ and raising the corruption.
The correct statement in this regard, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning.

This is because if corruption is made apparent, then it is apparent, and if it is apparent, then by making its appearance apparent, so in reading with one of the two readings there is clear evidence of the correctness of the meaning of the other.
As for the reading of or that it appears with the alif and with its deletion, then they are also close in meaning.

x: God the Almighty says: And Moses said to Pharaoh and his chiefs: “O my people, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant person who is too arrogant to believe in His Oneness, to acknowledge His Divinity, and to obey Him, and who does not believe in a Day when God will call His creation to account, and He will reward the good-doer for his good deeds and the evil-doer for his evil deeds.” Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, specifically sought refuge in God from those who do not believe in the Day of Judgment, because whoever does not truly believe in the Day of Judgment will not hope for reward for his good deeds, nor will he fear punishment for his evil deeds and wrongdoings. That is why he sought refuge from this type of people in particular.
And his saying:
h
And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said
, concealing his faith.
The scholars differed concerning this believing man.
Some of them said: He was from the people of Pharaoh, except that he had believed in Moses, and he kept his faith secret from Pharaoh and his people out of fear for himself.
Those who said this: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said

, he said: He is Pharaoh’s cousin, and it is said: He is the one who escaped with Moses. So whoever said this statement, and interpreted it this way, it is correct to stop if the reader wants to stop at his statement: from the family of Pharaoh, because that is a finished report that has been completed.

x: Others said: Rather, the man was an Israelite, but he was concealing his faith from the people of Pharaoh. According to this statement, the correct thing to say for those who want to stop is to stop at the statement concealing his faith, because his statement of the family of Pharaoh is a connection to his statement concealing his faith, so its completion is his statement concealing his faith. It has been mentioned that the name of this believing man from the family of Pharaoh was Gabriel, likewise.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq.
m: The more correct of the two opinions in my opinion is the one given by Al-Suddi, who said that the believing man was from the family of Pharaoh, who listened to his words and what he said, and refrained from killing Moses when he forbade him from killing him and said what he said, and said to him: I only show you what I see, and I only guide you to the path of righteousness. If he had been an Israelite, it would have been appropriate for the one who said what he said to him and his people to be punished for his words, because he did not seek advice from the Children of Israel, as he considered them his enemies, so how about his words about killing Moses if he had found a way! But since he was from the leaders of his people, he listened to what he said and refrained from what he was about to do to Moses. His statement:
h
Would you kill a man because he says

, ‘My Lord is God?’ means: Would you kill, O people, Moses because he says, ‘My Lord is God?’ “for” is in the accusative case for what it describes. And he has come to you with clear proofs, means: And he has come to you with clear signs that confirm the truth of what he says about that. And those clear proofs from the signs are his hand and his staff.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: And he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord, with his staff and his hand. And His statement:
h
And if he is a liar

, then upon him is his lie meaning: And if Moses was lying in his saying: God sent him to you to command you to worship Him and to abandon your religion that you are following, then the sin of his lie is upon him and not you. And if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you meaning: And if he was truthful in his saying, then what he promised you of punishment for your adherence to the religion that you are adhering to will befall you, so you have no need for you to kill him, lest you increase your Lord’s anger with you because of your disbelief. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar meaning: God does not guide to the truth one who transgresses and does what he is not supposed to do, a liar about Him, who lies and says falsehood and untruth about Him. The commentators differed on the meaning of extravagance mentioned by the believer in this passage.

x: Some of them said: He meant polytheism, and he meant: God does not guide one who associates partners with Him and slanders Him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar: a polytheist who has transgressed against himself by committing polytheism.

x: Others said: He meant someone who fights and sheds blood unjustly.
Mention of who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar. He said: The transgressor is the one who sheds blood, and it is said: They are the polytheists. The correct thing to say about this is: God informed us about this believer, saying, Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar. Polytheism is a type of transgression, and shedding blood unjustly is a type of transgression. Both of these things were combined in Pharaoh, so it is true that it should be general, just as God, the Most High, informed us about the one who said it, that he said that in general. And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said, "
h
Would you kill a man because he says
, 'My Lord is God,' and he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?
h
And if he is a liar
, then upon him is his lie. But if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will strike you. Indeed, God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar."

x: God the Almighty says, informing about what the believer from the family of Pharaoh said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:O my people, yours is the kingdom today, dominant in the land. Meaning: the land of Egypt. He says: Yours is the authority today and the kingdom is dominant over the Children of Israel in the land of Egypt. Then who will protect us from the wrath of God? He says: Who will repel from us the wrath and power of God if it befalls us, and His punishment if it comes to us? Pharaoh said: I only show you what I see. He says: Pharaoh said in response to this believer who forbade the killing of Moses: I only show you, O people, opinion and advice that I see to be good and right for myself and for you, and I only guide you to the path of righteousness. He says: I only call you to the path of truth and rightness in the matter of Moses and his killing, because if you do not kill him, your religion will be changed, and corruption will spread in your land.

God Almighty says: And the believer from the family of Pharaoh and his chiefs said: O my people, I fear for you, if you kill Moses, a day like the day of the parties who formed parties against the messengers of God, Noah, Hud, and Salih. God destroyed them because of their audacity towards them, so He will destroy you as He destroyed them.
And his people are
h
like the way of the people of Noah

meaning: He will do that to you and destroy you, just as He did to the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, and what He did to them. We have already explained the meaning of how often with evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it, along with mentioning the statements of the scholars of interpretation regarding it.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Like the habit of the people of Noah, meaning: like a situation.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Like the way of the people of Noah
, he said: Like what befell them. His saying:
h
And those after them means the people of Abraham and the people of Lot
, and they are also from the parties.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And those after them, he said: They are the parties. And His statement:
h
And God does not desire injustice for His servants

, the Most High says, informing about what the believer from the family of Pharaoh said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:God did not destroy these parties from these nations out of injustice from Him to them, without any crime they committed between themselves and Him, because He does not desire injustice for His servants, nor does He wish it, but He destroyed them because of their crimes and disbelief in Him, and their disobedience to His command.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what this believer said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:O my people, I fear for you because of your killing Moses if you kill him, the punishment of God on
h
the Day of Calling
. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement:
h
The Day of Calling
. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as
h
The Day of Calling

with a light dal and leaving out the proof of the ya’, in the sense of interaction, from the people called out, calling out, as He, the Most High, said: “And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, ‘We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’” (al-A’raf 7:44) And He said: And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Pour upon us some water.’ (al-A’raf 7:50) Therefore, the reciters of that interpreted it in this way.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada that he said
m: regarding this verse
h
The Day of Calling
he said: The day when the people of Hell call out to the people of Paradise: Pour water upon us.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And O my people
, indeed I fear for you
h
the Day of Calling

the day when the people of Paradise will call out to the people of Hell, “Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?” (al-A’raf 7:44) and the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise, Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you? (al-A’raf 7:50).

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
The Day of Calling

, he said: On the Day of Resurrection, the people of Paradise will call out to the people of Hell. “And it has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the meaning of this reading, with another interpretation in a different way.”

c: And this is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God will command Israfil to blow the first trumpet, and he will say: Blow the trumpet of terror, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except for whom God wills to continue it and prolong it so that it does not cease. And it is the one about which God says: And these do not wait except for a single blast that will have no reprieve
r
(Surah Sad: 15)

. So God will move the mountains and they will become a mirage, and the earth and its inhabitants will shake violently. And it is the one about which God says: The Day the great earthquake will shake, followed by another, hearts that Day will be trembling
r
(Surah al-Nazi’at 79:6-8)

. So it will be like a ship floundering in the sea, battered by the waves, tossing its inhabitants, or like a lamp hanging from the throne, shaken by the spirits, so the people will sway on its back, and the nursing mothers will be astray. Pregnant women will give birth, children will turn gray, and the devils will fly away until they reach the regions. The angels will meet them and strike their faces, and they will return, and people will turn back, calling out to one another. This is what God says: “
h
The Day of Calling

, the Day when you will turn back, retreating. You will have no protector from God.” According to this interpretation, the meaning of the words is: O my people, I fear for you the Day when people will call out to one another, from the terror of the blast of terror.

x: Others read it as: <
h
The Day of Calling
>with emphasis on the dal, meaning: the interaction from the word nad, and that is when they fled and scattered on the ground, as camels scattered: when they stray from their owners.
He mentioned who said that as well, and he mentioned the meaning intended by reading it as well:

c: Musa bin Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of al-Ajlah, who said:
m: I heard al-Dahhak bin Muzahim say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will command the lowest heaven to split open with its inhabitants, and the angels in it will descend, surrounding the earth and all that is on it, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they will be arranged in rows below each other. Then the highest angel will descend on its left side, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they will call out, and they will not come to any region of the earth except that they will find the seven rows of angels, so they will return to the place they were in. This is what God says: Indeed, I fear for you
h
the Day of Calling

, the Day when you will turn back and flee. This is what He says: And your Lord will come with angels, rank upon rank, and that Day Hell will be brought forth. (al-Fajr 89:22-23), and His statement: “O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not
h
And O my people
, indeed I fear for you
h
the Day of Calling

pass except by authority.” (al-Rahman: 33) ], and that is His saying: And the heaven will be split open, and that Day it will be fragile, and the angels will be over its corners. (al-Haqqah 69:16-17) Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Day of Calling
: He said: They will call out.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: that he read it as
h
The Day of Calling

with the ya’ and the dal pronounced with a light dal. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the reciters of the regions have done, which is to soften the dal and without adding the ya’. This is because this is the reading that is agreed upon by the reciters of the regions, and it is not permissible to contradict it in what it has transmitted. So if this is the correct reading, then the meaning of the statement is: O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day when people will call out to one another, either because of the horror of what they have witnessed of the great power of God, and the horror of what has befallen them of the distress of that day, or to remind some of them of God’s fulfillment of the promise that He promised them in this world, and a call for help from some of them to others because of the great affliction that they have encountered therein.

(al-A’raf 7:50) Therefore, the reciters of that interpreted it in this way.
