It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read it as The Day of Calling with the ya’ and the dal pronounced with a light dal.
The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the reciters of the regions have done, which is to soften the dal and without adding the ya’.
This is because this is the reading that is agreed upon by the reciters of the regions, and it is not permissible to contradict it in what it has transmitted.

So if this is the correct reading, then the meaning of the statement is: O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day when people will call out to one another, either because of the horror of what they have witnessed of the great power of God, and the horror of what has befallen them of the distress of that day, or to remind some of them of God’s fulfillment of the promise that He promised them in this world, and a call for help from some of them to others because of the great affliction that they have encountered therein.

x: "And His saying: "
h
On the Day when you turn your backs

, fleeing," its interpretation is based on the interpretation we mentioned from the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, "On the Day when they turn their backs, fleeing throughout the land, fearing God's punishment and chastisement when they see Hell." Its interpretation is the interpretation that Qatada said about the meaning of the Day of Calling: the day when you turn away from the place of reckoning to Hell. And in a manner similar to what was narrated from him, and from someone who said something similar to his statement regarding the meaning of the Day of Calling.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: On the Day you turn your backs: meaning, you will be taken to the Fire. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though what Qatada said on this matter is not far from the truth, and a group of people of interpretation said the same.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
On the Day you turn back
, fleeing he said: Fleeing, not escaping. His saying:
h
You have no protector from God
means:
h
You have no protector from God
to protect you, nor any supporter to aid you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
You have no protector from God
: meaning no helper. And His statement:
h
And he whom God leaves astray - for him there is no guide
. He means: And he whom God abandons and does not guide to the right path - for him there is no guide to guide him to it.

x: God Almighty says: And indeed, O my people, Joseph, son of Jacob, had come to you before Moses with clear proofs from God.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And Joseph had already come to you before, he said: before Moses. And His statement:
h
And you did not cease to be in doubt about that which he brought you

, meaning: You did not cease to be doubtful about that which Joseph brought you from your Lord, your hearts not being certain of its truth. Until when he perished, meaning: When Joseph died, you said, O people, God will not send to you after Joseph a messenger calling to the truth. “Thus does God send astray he who is a transgressor and doubtful,” meaning: Thus does God turn away from attaining the truth and seeking the path he who is a disbeliever in Him, doubtful, and skeptical about the truth of the report of His messengers.

x: God the Most High says, informing us about what the believers from the family of Pharaoh said: Those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them. So His statement, those who is a response to whoever in His statement: whoever is a transgressor. The interpretation of the statement is: Thus God misguides the people of extravagance and extremism in their misguidance by their disbelief in God and their boldness in disobeying Him, those who doubt the report of His messengers, those who dispute concerning the proofs that His messengers brought them in order to refute with falsehood the proofs without any authority that has come to them. He says: without a proof that came to them from their Lord, by which they refute the truth of the proofs that the messengers brought them. And those who if the meaning of the statement is what we mentioned is in the accusative case in response to whoever.
And His statement:
h
It is most hateful to God
means: That argument that they argue with about the verses of God is most hateful to God, and to those who believe in God. And the reason for His statement:
h
It is most hateful is because of the pronoun of argument in His statement
: It is most hateful and it is similar to His statement: It is a grave word that comes out of their mouths
r
(Al-Kahf 18:5)
. So He made the word in the accusative case from the one who made it in the accusative case, because He made in His statement:
h
It is most hateful the pronoun of their statement
: God has taken a son
r
(Al-Kahf 18:5)
. As for the one who did not make that implicit, then he raised the word. And His statement:
h
Thus does God set a seal upon every arrogant

, tyrannical heart. He says: Just as God has set a seal upon the hearts of the transgressors who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has been given to them, thus does God set a seal upon every heart that is arrogant towards God and rejects His Oneness and believes in His Messengers.

Tyrant: meaning one who is too proud to follow the truth. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions, except for Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, read it as upon every arrogant heart, adding the heart to the arrogant, meaning that God has set a seal on the hearts of all the arrogant. Whoever recited this, his saying
h
Jabbar was an adjective of arrogant
. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he used to recite this as: Thus does God set a seal on the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical person.

c: Ibn Yusuf told me that: Al-Qasim told us that Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Harun,
m: that it is like this in the script of Ibn Masʿud. This that was mentioned about Ibn Masʿud’s recitation confirms the recitation of those who read that by adding a qalb to al-mutakbir, because bringing each word forward before the qalb and delaying it after it does not change the meaning, rather the meaning is the same in both cases.

c: It was narrated from some Arabs by hearing:
m: He combs his hair every Friday, meaning: every Friday. As for Abu ʿAmr, he read that with the tanween of the qalb and left adding it to al-mutakbir, and made al-mutakbir and al-jabbar from the description of the qalb. The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it by adding the heart to the arrogant person, because arrogance is the action of the agent with his heart, just as if the killer killed someone, even if he killed him with his hand, then the action is attributed to him. The heart is one of the organs of the arrogant person, even if arrogance is in it, then the action is attributed to its agent, similar to what we said about killing. And even if it is as we said, the other is not rejected, because the Arabs do not prevent you from saying: The hand of so-and-so struck, and his eyes saw such-and-such, and his heart understood, so you attribute the actions to the organs, even if they are in reality for their owners.

Whoever recited this, his saying Jabbar was an adjective of arrogant.
It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he used to recite this as: Thus does God set a seal on the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical person.

As for Abu ʿAmr, he read that with the tanween of the qalb and left adding it to al-mutakbir, and made al-mutakbir and al-jabbar from the description of the qalb.

The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it by adding the heart to the arrogant person, because arrogance is the action of the agent with his heart, just as if the killer killed someone, even if he killed him with his hand, then the action is attributed to him.

x: God Almighty says: And when Pharaoh was admonished by the believer among his people with what he had admonished him with and warned him against killing Moses, the Prophet of God, and warned him of the punishment of God for saying, Will I kill him? what he had warned his minister, the evil minister Haman, about Pharaoh, he said, O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the causes. Meaning a building. We have already explained the meaning of a tower previously with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here. Perhaps I may reach the causes.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of causes in this place.
Some of them said: The causes of the heavens are their paths.
Those who said that: Ahmad bin Hisham told us, he said:

c: Abdullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh, The causes of the heavens he said:
m: The paths of the heavens.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The most eloquent of causes are the causes of the heavens. He said: The paths of the heavens.

x: Others said: What is meant by the causes of the heavens is the gates of the heavens.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And Pharaoh said, ‘O Haman, build for me a tower.’ He was the first to build with this brick and bake it, that I may reach the ways * the ways of the heavens: meaning the gates of the heavens.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the heavenly abode.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Perhaps I may reach the causes * The causes of the heavens

he said: The abode of heaven. We have previously explained that the cause is everything that leads to reaching what is sought, such as a rope, ladder, path, etc. The most correct statement about this is to say: Its meaning is that I may reach, from the causes of the heavens, causes by which I may see the God of Moses, whether those causes were paths, or doors, or houses, or something else. And his saying:
h
So he looked up to the God of Moses
. The reciters differed in their reading of his saying:
h
So he looked up
. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as
h
So he looked up
with a damma on the ‘ayn, in response to his saying: He reached the causes and in conjunction with it. It was mentioned on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj that he read
h
So he looked up

in the accusative case in response to Ali. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some of the Arabs recited to him: On the vicissitudes of time or its states The gathering guides us from its gatherings So the soul rests from its sighs So, we put Fattasartah as an answer to Al-'Ala. The reading that I do not permit other than it is the raising of the voice in this regard, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it. And his saying:
h
And I think he is a liar
means: I think Moses is a liar in what he says and claims that he has a Lord in heaven who sent him to us. And His statement:
h
And thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh

, God Almighty says: And thus God made the evil of his deeds attractive to Pharaoh when he rebelled against Him, until his soul tempted him to reach the heavens, in order to look up to the God of Moses. His saying:
h
And he was prevented from the path
. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it:
h
And he was prevented from the path
, with a damma on the sad, in a way that does not name the agent.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And he was turned away from the path. He said: He did that to him, made his evil deeds seem attractive to him, and turned him away from the path. Hamid, Abu Amr, and most of the Basra reciters read it as <wasd>with a fat-ha on the sad, meaning: Pharaoh turned away from the path of God with which Moses was sent, out of arrogance. The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement:
h
And the plot of Pharaoh was only in vain

. God Almighty says: And the plot of Pharaoh, who plotted to find out about the God of Moses, was only in loss, loss of wealth, and deception, because his expenditure on the palace was wasted in vain, and he did not obtain anything of what he wanted with what he spent. So that is loss and vain.

x: Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And the plot of Pharaoh was only in ruin
means: in loss.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of The causes of the heavens, so he looked at the God of Moses, and indeed, I think he is a liar. And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deeds, and he was prevented from the way. And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin. Mujahid, regarding his statement: In ruins, he said: Loss.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the plot of Pharaoh was only in ruin
, meaning: in misguidance and loss.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And Pharaoh’s plot was nothing but destruction
, he said: Destruction and misguidance are one and the same.

The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as So he looked up with a damma on the ‘ayn, in response to his saying: He reached the causes and in conjunction with it.
The reading that I do not permit other than it is the raising of the voice in this regard, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it.
The reciters differed in their recitation of that.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it: And he was prevented from the path, with a damma on the sad, in a way that does not name the agent.
Hamid, Abu Amr, and most of the Basra reciters read it as <wasd>with a fat-ha on the sad, meaning: Pharaoh turned away from the path of God with which Moses was sent, out of arrogance.

x: God Almighty says, informing about the believer in God from the people of Pharaoh: And the one who believed said from the people of Pharaoh to his al-Nas 114:O my people, follow me and I will guide you to the path of right conduct. He says: If you follow me and accept what I say to you, I will show you the path of righteousness by which you will be guided if you take it and follow it. And that is the religion of God with which Moses was sent.

He says: This worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment. He says to his al-Nas 114:This fleeting worldly life that has been hastened for you in this abode is only a temporary enjoyment that you enjoy until a term you reach, then you die and it is taken away from you. And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement. He says: And indeed, the Hereafter, which is the home of settlement in which you will settle and will not die nor will it be taken away from you, He says: So know about it, and seek it. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement. Paradise has settled with its people, and Hell has settled with its people.

x: He says: Whoever commits a sin against God in this worldly life, God will not reward him in the Hereafter except with an evil like it, and that is by punishing him for it, And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female He says: And whoever acts in obedience to God in this world, and obeys His command, and refrains from what He has forbidden them, whether male or female, and he is a believer in God, These will enter Paradise He says: So those who do that from among God’s servants will enter Paradise in the Hereafter. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Whoever does a bad deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof meaning polytheism. According to Qatada, a bad deed is polytheism. And whoever does a righteous deed meaning good whether male or female, while he is a believer. His statement,
h
They will be provided therein without account
, means: God will provide them in Paradise from its fruits, and from its pleasures and delights without account.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: They will be provided for therein without account. He said: No, by God, there is no measure or scale for you.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what this believer said to his unbelieving al-Nas 114:
h
Why do I call you to salvation

from God’s torment and punishment by believing in Him, following His Messenger Moses, and believing in what he brought you from his Lord, and you call me to the Fire? He says: And you call me to do the deeds of the people of the Fire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

h

? He said: Belief in God.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Why do I call you to salvation
and you call me to the Fire? He said: This is the believer of Pharaoh’s family. He said: They call him to their religion and to reside with them.

x: And his saying: You call me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, meaning: And I associate with God in His worship idols, and I do not know that it is appropriate for me to worship them and associate them in the worship of God, because God did not permit me to do that with information or reason. And His statement:
h
And I invite you to the Exalted in Might

, the Forgiving, meaning: And I invite you to worship the Exalted in Might in His vengeance upon those who disbelieve in Him, who is not prevented from anything when He takes vengeance upon an enemy of His, the Forgiving of those who repent to Him after disobeying Him, for His pardon of them, so nothing can harm them with His pardon of them. He says: So this is the one whose description is this, so worship, and do not worship that from whom there is no harm or benefit.

He says: Truly, the idols you call me to have no supplication in this world or in the hereafter, because they are inanimate objects that do not speak and do not understand anything. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
He has no supplication in this world
, he said: The idol is nothing.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
He has no supplication in this world or in the Hereafter
: meaning he neither benefits nor harms.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has no supplication in this world or in the Hereafter
. And His statement:
h
And that our return is to God
means: And that our return and our turning back after our death is to God.
h
And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire

means: And that the polytheists who transgressed His limits, the murderers of souls that God has forbidden to be killed, are the companions of the Fire of Hell when we return to God. In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, with their differences, about the meaning of the extravagant in this place.

x: Some of them said: They are the ones who shed blood unjustly.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire
, he said: Those who shed blood unjustly.

m: regarding the words of God:
h
And the transgressors
are the companions of the Fire, he said: They are those who shed blood unjustly.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And the transgressors
he said: Those who shed blood unjustly, they are the people of the Fire.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire
, he said: God called them transgressors, Pharaoh and those with him.

x: Others said: They are the polytheists.
Those who said this: Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the transgressors

are the companions of the Fire: meaning the polytheists. We have already explained the meaning of transgression before in a sufficient manner so that it is not necessary to repeat it here. We chose the interpretation of this in this place as we chose, because the one who said this statement to Pharaoh and his people intended Pharaoh for his disbelief, and what he intended to do in killing Moses, and Pharaoh was arrogant and violent in his disbelief in God, shedding blood that was forbidden to him to shed, and all of that is extravagance, so we chose what we chose of the interpretation in that.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what the believer from the family of Pharaoh said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:Then you will remember, O people, when you witness the punishment of God that has befallen you and you have encountered what you have encountered, the truth of what I say, and the reality of what I have informed you of, that the transgressors are the people of the Fire.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Then you will remember what I say to you
, so I said to him: Is that in the Hereafter? He said: Yes. His saying:
h
And I entrust my affair to God

means: I submit my affair to God, I entrust it to Him and I put my trust in Him, for He is sufficient for whoever puts his trust in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And I entrust my affair to God

, he said: I place my affair in God’s hands. His saying: Indeed, God is All-Seeing of His servants means that God knows the affairs of His servants, who among them is obedient and who is disobedient to Him, who deserves a beautiful reward and who deserves a bad punishment.

x: And His statement: So God saved him from
h
the evils of their plotting

. God Almighty says: So God saved this believer from the family of Pharaoh, through his faith and belief in His Messenger Moses, from the evil of the torment and affliction that Pharaoh inflicted upon those who disagreed with him, so He saved him from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The evils of their plotting

He said: He was a Copt from the people of Pharaoh, and he was saved with Moses. He said: It was mentioned to us that he was walking in front of Moses on that day and saying: Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of God? He said: In front of you. The believer said to him: Is there anything in front of me except the sea? Moses said: No, by God, I have neither lied nor been lied to. Then he walked for a while and said: Where have you been commanded, O Prophet of God? He said: In front of you. He said: Is there anything in front of me except the sea? He said: No, by God, I have neither lied nor been lied to, until he came to the sea and struck it with his staff, and it split into twelve paths, one path for each tribe. His statement:
h
And the worst of punishment befell Pharaoh’s family
means: It befell Pharaoh’s family and was imposed upon them. What is meant by Pharaoh’s family in this passage are his followers and the obedient people among his people.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement of God: And the worst of punishment befell Pharaoh’s people, he said: The people of Pharaoh. What he meant by his saying:
h
The worst of the torment is the torment of God that they suffered
, which is the fire of Hell.

x: God Almighty says, explaining the severity of the punishment that befell these wretched people of Pharaoh: That which befell them of the severity of God’s punishment the Fire, they will be exposed to it. When they perished and God drowned them, their souls were placed in the bodies of black birds, and they will be exposed to the Fire twice a day, morning and evening, until the Hour comes.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Qais, on the authority of al-Hudhayl bin Shurahbil, he said:
m: The souls of the family of Pharaoh are in the bellies of black birds that come and go to the fire, and that is its width.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: It has reached me that the souls of Pharaoh’s people are in the bellies of black birds, exposed to the fire morning and evening, until the Hour comes. Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair narrated: Hammad bin Muhammad Al-Fazari Al-Balkhi narrated: I heard Al-Awza’i being asked by a man, who said: May God have mercy on you, we saw birds emerging from the sea, heading towards the west, egg-white, in groups, and only God knows their number. Then, in the evening, a similar number would return black. He said: Did you realize that? They said: Yes. He said: Those birds have in their crops the souls of Pharaoh’s family, exposed to the Fire morning and evening. They return to their nests with their feathers burned and turned black, and at night white feathers grow on them, and the black ones scatter. Then they go out in the morning and are exposed to the Fire morning and evening, then they return to their nests. That is their habit in this world. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, God says: Enter Pharaoh’s family into the severest punishment. They said: And they used to say: They were six hundred thousand fighters.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Harmalah told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Hamid, he said:
m: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi say: There is no night nor half a day in the Hereafter, but rather it is morning and evening, and that is in the Qur’an regarding the people of Pharaoh: They will be presented to it morning and evening. And likewise it was said to the people of Paradise: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening.
r
(Maryam 19:62)
It was said: What is meant by that is that they will be shown their homes in Hell as torture for them morning and evening.

x: Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Fire will be shown to them morning and evening. He said: They will be shown to it morning and evening, and it will be said to them: O family of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings, as a rebuke, punishment, and humiliation for them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: morning and evening, he said: What was the world?

c: The most correct of the sayings is that God has informed us that
m: the people of Pharaoh will be exposed to the Fire in the morning and the evening. It is possible that this exposure to the Fire will be in the manner we mentioned from Al-Hudhayl and those who said something similar, or it may be as Qatadah said. However, there is no report that necessitates the argument that this is what is meant, for there is nothing in that except what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, which is that they will be exposed to the Fire in the morning and the evening. The root of morning and evening is a source that has been made into times.
b.via: most correct of the sayings is that God has

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say about this: It is a verbal noun, just as you say: I came to him in the dark, making it a circumstance and it is a verbal noun. He said: If you had said: Your appointment is tomorrow, or your appointment is dark, and raised it, just as you say: Your appointment is on Friday, it would not be good, because these verbal nouns and the like, such as sahar, are only made into circumstance. He said: All circumstance is not established. The grammarians of Kufa said: It is not heard at these times, even if they are verbal nouns, except in the Arabization, Your appointment is the day of your appointment, morning and evening, as God Almighty said: Its morning is a month and its evening is a month Saba’ 34:12, so it was raised. They mentioned that they heard: The two cloaks are two months, and they said: The indefinite nouns are not heard at all except in the nominative case, except for their saying: Your generosity is only sometimes.
They said: This is only permissible because it means: Your generosity is only now and then. So since its interpretation is an addition, it is accusative. And His statement:
h
And on the Day the Hour comes

, admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. The reciters differed in reading that. The majority of reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, except for Asim The Fire will be exposed to them morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour appears, [it will be said], "Admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment." and Abu Amr, read it as
h
And on the Day the Hour comes

, admit the people of Pharaoh with a fat-ha on the alif of adkhalwa in connection and disconnection, meaning: the order to enter them into the Fire. If it is read in this way, the al is in the accusative case because adkhalwa falls before it. Asim and Abu Amr read it as
h
and on the Day the Hour comes
, enter with a connected alif and its omission in connection from the word, and with a damma if it is started after a pause on al-sa'ah.

If someone reads it in this way, the al according to his reading is in the accusative case as a call, because the meaning of the speech according to his reading is: Enter, O people of Pharaoh, into the severest punishment. The correct thing to say about this in my opinion is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, and each of them has been recited by a group of reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites is correct. So the meaning of the statement then is:
h
And on the Day the Hour comes

, it will be said to the family of Pharaoh, Enter, O family of Pharaoh, into the severest punishment. This is according to the reading of the one who connected the alif of idkhulū and did not cut it off. Its meaning according to the other reading is:
h
And on the Day the Hour comes
, God will say to His angels, Enter the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.

The correct thing to say about this in my opinion is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, and each of them has been recited by a group of reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites is correct.
This is according to the reading of the one who connected the alif of idkhulū and did not cut it off.
Its meaning according to the other reading is: And on the Day the Hour comes, God will say to His angels, Enter the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And warn them of the approaching Day when hearts will be at the throats, stifling. “And when they will dispute in the Fire.” He says: And when they will argue in the Fire. What is meant by that is: When those whom the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was commanded to warn from among the polytheists of his people will argue in the Fire. The weak among them, who are those followed in associating partners with God, will say to their leaders who followed them in misguidance: Indeed, we were your followers in this world in disbelief in God. “So can you relieve us today of a portion of the Fire?” They mean a portion, so that you may lighten it for us, for we used to hasten to love you in this world, and before you we came. If it were not for you, we would have been believers in this world, and this calamity would not have befallen us today. According to some Basra grammarians, the verb tabi'a can be singular or plural, while according to some Kufa grammarians, it can be plural without a singular because it is like a verbal noun. He said: If you wish, its singular can be tabi'a, so it would be like kha'il and khawul, and gha'ib and ghaib.

The correct thing to say about that, in my opinion, is that it is the plural of the singular form of follower, but it may be possible that it is singular, in which case it would be the plural of followers.

c: So those who were followed answered them with what God had informed them
m: about. Those who were arrogant said, and they are the leaders who were followed in misguidance in this world: “O people, we and you are all in this Fire, abiding eternally. We have no escape from it. “Indeed, God has judged between the servants” with the decisiveness of His judgment. He has settled the people of Paradise in Paradise and the people of Hell in Hell. We will not leave what we are in of affliction, nor will they return from what is in it of bliss. He raised His statement: all with His statement: in it and did not place it in the accusative case as an adjective. There is disagreement over the permissibility of the accusative in this regard in speech.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: If kull is not added, then following is not permissible.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: This is permissible in deletion and non-deletion, because if their nouns are deleted, it is sufficient from them. We have already explained the correct opinion on this matter in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

God the Most High says: “And the people of Hell will say to its keepers and guardians, seeking their help from the great affliction they are in, and hoping that they will find relief from them: ‘Call upon your Lord’ for us to lighten for us one day’, meaning the amount of one day of the days of this world, ‘of the torment’ that we are in. We only said that the meaning of that is the amount of one day of the days of this world, because the Hereafter is a day in which there is no night, and it is said: Lighten for them one day.
And His statement:
h
They will say

, ‘Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?’ God Almighty says: The keepers of Hell will say to them, Did not your messengers come to you in this world with clear proofs of the Oneness of God, so that you would affirm His Oneness and believe in Him, and disavow all deities besides Him?
h
They will say

, Yes, our messengers did bring us that. And His saying: They said, ‘Then call upon Him.’ God Almighty says: The keepers said to them: Then call upon your Lord, to whom the messengers came with the call to faith in Him. And His statement:
h
And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but error

, meaning: They have supplicated, and their supplication is nothing but error, because it is a supplication that does not benefit them, and is not answered. Rather, it is said to them: Be gone into it, disgraced, and do not speak to it (al-Mu’minun 23:108).

Someone says: What is the meaning of Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world? We know that some of them were killed by their enemies and mutilated, such as Isaiah, John the son of Zechariah and their likes.

Some of them were intended to be killed by their people, but the best thing for them was to be saved from them until they left them, saving themselves, such as Abraham who migrated from his land to Syria, leaving his people, and Jesus who was raised to the heavens when his people wanted to kill him.

c: So where is the support that He told us
m: He would support His messengers and those who believe in Him in this life, when these prophets of His had suffered from their people what you know, and were not supported against those who suffered what He did to them? It was said: His statement Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world has two meanings, both of which are correct. One of them is that its meaning is: “Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in this worldly life, either by making them superior over those who deny Us and by giving them victory, until they subjugate them completely and humiliate them completely, as We did with David and Solomon, giving them such kingdom and authority with which they subjugated every disbeliever, and as We did with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by making him victorious over those among his people who denied him. Or by taking revenge on those who opposed and opposed them by destroying them and saving the messengers from those who denied and opposed them, as We did with Noah and his people, by drowning his people and saving him from them, and as We did with Moses, Pharaoh and his people, when He drowned them and saved Moses and those who believed in him from the Children of Israel and others, and so on. Or by Our taking revenge in this worldly life from their deniers after the death of Our Messenger, after their destruction, as We did in giving aid to Isaiah after his destruction, by giving authority over his killers to those We gave authority to until We were victorious through them over his killers, and as We did with the killers of John, by giving authority to Nebuchadnezzar over them until We were victorious through him over his killer, and as We gave aid to Jesus over those who wanted to kill him among the Romans until We destroyed them through them. This is one of its two aspects.
b.via: So where is the support that He

x: Some of the people of interpretation have directed the meaning of that to this aspect.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement of God: “Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world.” The prophets and believers were killed in this world and they were victorious. This is because the nation that does that to the prophets and believers will not go away until God sends a people through whom He will support those who were killed among them. The other interpretation is that this statement is in the form of a report on behalf of all of the messengers and believers, and the intended meaning is one, so the interpretation of the statement in that case is “Indeed, We will support Our Messenger Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those who believe in him during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand,” as we explained previously that the Arabs convey the report in the form of the plural, and the intended meaning is one if they do not appoint a specific person for the report. The reciters differed in their reading of the verse: And the Day the witnesses will stand * The Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as and the Day he stands with a ya’, and benefits also with a ya’.

x: Some of the people of Mecca and some of the reciters of Basra read it as taqwam with a ta’, and tanfa’ with a ta’. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. We have previously explained that the Arabs use the plural of the male verb and make it feminine if it is preceded by something that makes repeating it unnecessary. What is meant by His statement,
h
And the Day the witnesses will stand is the day when the witnesses from among the angels

, prophets, and believers will stand against the nations who denied their messengers, testifying that the messengers delivered to them the messages of their Lord, and that the nations denied them. Witnesses is the plural of martyr, just as ashraf is the plural of sharif.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the Day when the witnesses will stand from among the angels of God, His prophets, and the believers in Him.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the Day when the witnesses will stand means the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said:
m: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day the witnesses will stand.

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And the Day the witnesses will stand, he said: The angels.

x: And His statement:
h
Their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers

. God Almighty says: That is a day when the polytheists’ excuses will not benefit them, because they will not apologize if they apologize except with falsehood. This is because God has excused them in this world and accepted their arguments in it, so they will have no excuse in the Hereafter except clinging to falsehood by saying: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. (al-An’am 6:23) His statement: And for them is the curse, meaning: For the wrongdoers is the curse, which is distance from God’s mercy. And for them is the worst home, meaning: And for them, along with the curse from God, is the worst of what is in the Hereafter, which is the painful torment.

God Almighty says: And We gave Moses the clarification of the truth with which We sent him, just as We gave it to Muhammad, but Pharaoh and his people denied it, just as Quraysh denied Muhammad. And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture meaning: We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Torah, so We taught it to them and sent it down to them. As guidance meaning as clarification of the matter of their religion and the obligations We imposed on them. And as a reminder for those of understanding meaning: And as a reminder from Us to those of wisdom and intellects among them of it.
Guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
And His statement: "
h
So be patient
. Indeed, the promise of God is true." God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:
h
So be patient

, O Muhammad, for the command of your Lord, and carry out the message He has sent you with, and convey to your people and to whomever you have been commanded to convey what has been revealed to you, and be certain of the truth of the promise of God which He promised you of supporting you and supporting whoever believes in you and believes in you against whoever denies you and rejects what you have brought to him from your Lord. Indeed, the promise of God is true and He will not break it, and He will fulfill it. And seek forgiveness for your sin means: Ask Him to forgive your sins and pardon you for them. And glorify the praises of your Lord means: Connect with thanks to your Lord. In the evening means from the time the sun passes its zenith until nightfall.
And in the early morning means from the rising of the second dawn until sunrise.

Some people have interpreted in the early morning as meaning from sunrise until the time of forenoon has passed, but the first statement is well-known among the Arabs. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the conjunction of Ibkar and Ba’ not being good for it to be used in it after Ashi the evening, but Ba’ is good in it.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of that is: And glorify the praises of your Lord in the evening and in the morning. He said: It may be said: Zayd is in the house, meaning: Zayd is in the house.
Another said: It was said thus because the meaning of the statement is: Praise be to God at these two times and at these two times, by inserting Ba’ in both of them and in one of them.

God Almighty says: Indeed, those who dispute with you, O Muhammad, concerning the signs that you have brought them from your Lord without any authority that has come to them - meaning, without any proof that has come to them from God in their dispute with you concerning them -
h
there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance
- meaning,
h
there is nothing in their hearts except arrogance

, because of which they are too proud to follow you and accept the truth that you have brought them, out of envy for the favor that God has given you and the honor that He has honored you with in the form of prophethood - they will not attain it - meaning, what they have envied you for is something that they will not be able to comprehend or attain, because that is God’s favor that He gives to whomever He wills and it is not something that can be attained through wishful thinking. It has been said that its meaning is: there is nothing in their hearts except pride, and they will not attain that greatness because God has humiliated them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
There is nothing in their hearts except arrogance

, he said: greatness. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them, the people of interpretation said.

x: Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them means that no authority has come to them for that. And His statement: “
h
So seek refuge in God
. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.” God Almighty says:
h
So seek refuge in God

, O Muhammad, from the evil of those who dispute about the verses of God without authority, and it is arrogance for any of it to occur in your heart. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He says: Indeed, God is the All-Hearing of what these disputants say about the verses of God and others of the words of the All-Seeing of what their limbs do, nothing of that is hidden from Him.

x: God Almighty says: The creation of the heavens and the earth and their establishment without anything is greater, O people, in your opinion, if you think the creation of people and their establishment without anything is greater than the creation of people. But most people do not know that the creation of all of that is easy for God.

The blind man who does not see anything is not the same as the unbeliever who does not contemplate God’s proofs with his eyes, ponder them and consider them, so that he knows His Oneness and His ability to create whatever He wills, and believes in Him and acknowledges Him. And the one who sees with his eyes what they see and perceives, and this is an example of the believer who sees with his eyes the proofs of God, so he ponders them and is admonished, and knows what they indicate of the Oneness of his Creator and the greatness of His power and His ability to create what He wills. Nor are the disbelievers and the believers equal. And those who believe and do righteous deeds God, the Most High, says: Nor are the believers in God and His Messenger, who are obedient to their Lord, equal to the wrongdoer, who is the disbeliever in his Lord, disobeys Him, and opposes His command. Little do you remember God, the Most High, says: Little do you remember, O people, the proofs of God, so you take heed and take heed.

He says: If you remembered His signs and took heed, you would know the error of what you are persisting upon, of your denial of God’s ability to revive those of His creation who have perished after perishing, and to restore them to life after their death, and you would know the ugliness of your polytheism of those you associate with Him in the worship of your Lord. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, You remember. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as <you remember>with a ya' as a statement. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as <you remember>with a ta' as an address. The opinion in this regard is that both readings are correct.

x: God Almighty says: The Hour in which God will revive the dead for reward and punishment will come, O people. There is no doubt about its coming. He says: So be certain of its coming, and that you will be resurrected after your death and rewarded for your deeds, so repent to your Lord. But most people do not believe. He says: But most of the Quraysh do not believe in its coming.
And His statement:
h
And your Lord says
h
Call upon Me
; I will respond to you.’ God Almighty says:
h
And your Lord says
, O people,
h
call upon Me

. He says: “Worship Me and devote your worship to Me alone, without those you worship besides Me, such as idols and statues and other things. “I will respond to you.” He says: I will answer your call, so I will pardon you and have mercy on you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

m: his statement:
h
Call upon Me
, I will answer you means: Make Me alone, and I will forgive you.

m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Supplication is worship. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘
h
And your Lord says
h
Call upon Me
; I will respond to you.” Indeed, those who disdain My worship…’” Muhammad ibn Bashar told us:

m: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Supplication is worship, ‘
h
And your Lord says

; I will respond to you”… the verse.”

h
And your Lord says

; I will respond to you.’”

m: may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar chain of transmission.

h

; I will respond to you.” Indeed, those who disdain My worship…’” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me:

Then he recited this verse: ‘And your Lord says, “Call upon Me; I will respond to you.”

x: God Almighty says: God, to whom divinity is the only one worthy of worship, and to whom worship is not due except Him, whose description is that He has made for you, O people, a dwelling place to dwell in, so that you may be at peace from the actions and disturbances of livelihood, and the causes that you used to act in during your day. And the day is seeing. He says: And He made the day seeing from those who are disturbed in it for their livelihood, and seeking their needs. A blessing from Him in that to you. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind. He says: God is generous to you, O people, with bounty that is unmatched. But most people are not grateful. He says: But most of them do not thank Him through obedience to Him, and sincerity in divinity and worship of Him, nor has He done any favor for which He deserves thanks from Him.

God Almighty says: The One who did these deeds and bestowed these blessings upon you, O people, is God, the Master of your affairs and the One who will reform your affairs. He is your Creator and the Creator of everything. There is no god but Him means: There is no deity worthy of worship other than Him. Then how are you deluded? means: What direction do you take and where do you go from Him, so that you worship other than Him?

And His statement: Thus are those who used to deny the signs of God deluded. He says: Just as you, O people, have turned away from it, and have turned away from the truth to falsehood, and from guidance to misguidance, those nations who were before you turned away from the signs of God, meaning: they used to deny the proofs and evidence of God and did not believe. He says: So you, the Quraysh, have followed their path and embarked on their path of misguidance.

God Almighty says: God to whom divinity is exclusive, O people, is He who made for you the earth on whose surface you live a settlement on which you settle and dwell above it, and the sky a structure: He built it and raised it above you without pillars that you can see for your interests and the sustenance of your worldly life until you reach your appointed times. And He shaped you and perfected your shapes meaning: He created you and perfected your creation. And He provided for you from the good things meaning: He provided for you from lawful sustenance and delicious foods and drinks. And His statement: That is God, your Lord, meaning, the Most High says: The One who performed these actions and bestowed these blessings upon you, O people, is God, to whom divinity is the only one worthy of being worshipped, and your Lord, to whom no other Lordship is suitable, not the One who neither benefits nor harms, nor creates nor provides. So blessed be God, Lord of the worlds, meaning: So blessed be God, the Owner of all creation, jinn and humans, and all other kinds of creation besides them.

He is the Ever-Living means He is the Ever-Living who does not die, the Ever-Living, and everything other than Him is transient and not eternal. There is no god but Him means: There is no true deity whose worship is permissible, and for whom divinity is fit, except God, who has these attributes.
h
So call upon Him

, O people, making your religion sincere for Him, making your obedience sincere for Him, singling out divinity for Him alone. Do not associate anything in His worship other than Him, or any idol or statue, and do not make for Him a rival or equal. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds means: Thanks are due to God, who is the Owner of all kinds of creation, from angels, jinn, humans, and others, not to the gods and idols who do not own anything, and are not able to harm or benefit, rather He is owned. If someone harms Him, He is not able to repel it from Himself.
A group of scholars used to order whoever said There is no god but God to follow it with Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, interpreting this verse as a command from God to say that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told me, he said:
m: I heard my father, he said: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whoever says there is no god but God, let him say after it: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, for that is His saying: “
h
So call upon Him
, devoting your religion to Him alone. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”
b.via: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: If one of you says: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, then let him say: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Then he said: “
h
So call upon Him
, making your religion sincere to Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: that he used to prefer that when he said: There is no god but God, he should follow it with: Praise be to God, then he would recite this verse: “He is the Ever-Living; there is no god but Him,
h
so call upon Him
, devoting your religion to Him sincerely. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”

c: Muhammad ibn Amara told me: Ubayd God ibn Musa told us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: If one of you says, There is no god but God alone, then let him say after it, Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Then he recites, “
h
So call upon Him
, devoting your religion to Him alone. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”

evidence.text: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, that he used to prefer that when he said: There is no god but God, he should follow it with: Praise be to God, then he would recite this verse: “He is the Ever-Living; there is no god but Him, so call upon Him, devoting your religion to Him sincerely.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people from Quraysh, I have been forbidden, O people, to worship those you invoke besides God, of gods and idols, when the clear proofs came to me from my Lord, meaning: when the clear signs came to me from my Lord, and those are the verses of the Book of God that He revealed. And I was commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds, meaning: And my Lord commanded me to humble myself before the Lord of all things and the Owner of all creation, in submission, and to submit to Him in obedience, not to anything else.

God Almighty says, commanding His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to alert the polytheists of his people to His arguments against them regarding His Oneness: Say, O Muhammad, to your al-Nas 114:I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the Worlds, Whose description are these attributes, which are that He created your father Adam from dust, then He created you from a sperm-drop, then from a clot “after you were sperm-drops,” then He brings you forth as a child from the wombs of your mothers as children, then that you may reach your full strength, so that your strength is perfected, your youth is completed, and your creation is complete as old men. And among you is he who dies before reaching old age. And that you may reach a specified term meaning: And that you may reach a specific appointed time for your life, and a limited term that you do not exceed, nor advance before. “And that you may understand” meaning: And that you may understand God’s arguments against you with that, and ponder His signs and know by them that there is no god but Him. He did that. .

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad, It is He who gives life and causes death. He says, “Say to them: And among His attributes, may His praise be glorified, is that He is the One who gives life to whomever He wills after his death, and causes death to whomever He wills of the living after his life.” <And when He decrees a matter>He says: And when He decrees the coming into being of one of the matters that He wants to bring into being, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ meaning to the one He wants to bring into being, Be, and so what He wants to bring into being comes into being without any effort or expense.
And His statement,
h
Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the verses of God
h
How are they turned away

? He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, these polytheists among your people, who dispute with you concerning the proofs and verses of God? “
h
How are they turned away
? He is saying: In what way are they turned away from the truth and deviated from the right path?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
How are they turned away
?: How are they lying and being just?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
How are they turned away
? He said: They are turned away from the truth.

x: The interpreters differed about who was meant by this verse.
Some of them said: It meant the people of destiny.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said:
m: If this verse was not revealed about the Qadarites, then I do not know about whom it was revealed:
h
Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the verses of God - how they are turned away
? to His saying: “We did not call upon anything before. Thus does God mislead the disbelievers.”

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said:
m: If the people of destiny are not those who delve into the verses of God, then we have no knowledge of it.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Malik bin Abi Al-Khair Al-Ziyadi told me, on the authority of Abu Qabil, he said: Uqba bin Amir Al-Juhani told me,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The People of the Book and the people of leniency will perish from among my nation.’ Uqba said: ‘O Messenger of God, who are the People of the Book?’ He said: ‘A people who learn the Book of God and argue with those who believe.’ Uqba said: ‘O Messenger of God, and who are the people of leniency?’ He said: ‘A people who follow their desires and neglect their prayers.’” Abu Qabil said: “I do not think that the deniers of predestination are anyone other than those who argue with those who believe. As for the people of leniency, I do not think that they are anyone other than the people of the pillar who have no imam or congregation over them, and they do not know the month of Ramadan.”

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the polytheists.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the verses of God - how they are turned away

? He said: These are the polytheists. The correct statement about this is what Ibn Zayd said, and God made clear the truth of this by saying: Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers.

x: God the Most High says: Have you not seen those who dispute about the verses of God? How they are turned away those who deny the Book of God, which is this Qur’an? The second those is in the accusative case in response to the first those as a description. And that with which We sent Our messengers He says: And they also denied, along with their denial of the Book of God, that with which We sent Our messengers, of sincere worship to God, and disavowal of what is worshipped besides Him of deities and rivals, and acknowledgment of the resurrection after death for reward and punishment. And His statement: And they will know * When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, this is a threat from God to those who associate others with Him. God, the Most High, says: Then those who dispute concerning the verses of God, who deny the Book, will know the truth of what you tell them, O Muhammad, and the truth of what they are denying today of this Book, when the shackles and chains are placed around their necks in Hell.
The regions and chains have been read in the nominative case in apposition to the shackles, in accordance with the meaning I explained.

c: It was reported from Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to read it: And the chains are dragged with the chains in the accusative case in the boiling water. It was also reported from him that he used to say: It is only while they are dragged in chains. Scholars of Arabic do not permit the subject to be in the genitive case when the preposition is implied.

x: Some of them used to say in this regard: If someone were to imagine that he said: The meaning is only: When their necks are dragged in the shackles and chains, then the chains would be in the genitive case according to this school of thought. He said: Similar to what has been returned to the meaning is the saying of the poet: The snake's foot and the bravest of snakes have made peace with him. So he put the brave man and the snakes before that in the nominative case, because the meaning is that his foot made peace with the snakes and he made peace with them, so when he needed to put the rhyme in the accusative case, he made the verb from the foot apply to the snakes. The correct reading for us in this regard is what the readers of the regions have said, due to the consensus of the authorities on it, which is to raise the chains in conjunction with what is mentioned in His statement: on their necks of the mention of shackles.

His saying: They will be dragged means: These people who denied the Book in this world will be dragged by the guards of punishment on the Day of Resurrection into the boiling water, which is the heat of which has reached its peak and reached its limit.
