And his saying:
h
Then they will be burned in the Fire
means:
h
Then they will be burned in the Fire
of Hell. He says Hell will be burned with them: that is, it will be kindled with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: They will be kindled, he said: A fire will be lit for them.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Then they will be burned in the Fire
. He said: They will be burned in the Fire.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Then they will be lit in the Fire
, he said: They will be lit in the Fire: it will be kindled for them in it.

x: And His statement: Then it will be said to them, ‘Where are those you used to associate * with God?’ He says: Then it will be said: Where are those you used to associate with God by worshipping them, your gods and idols, so that they may aid you and rescue you from the affliction and torment you are in? For the worshipped One aids His servant and His servant. This is said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke for what they did in this world of disbelief in God and obedience to Satan. Then the poor people responded and said: They have gone astray from us. He said: They turned away from us, so they took a path other than ours, and left us in this affliction. Rather, they have not gone astray from us, but we did not call upon anything before in this world. God, the Most High, says: Thus does God lead astray the disbelievers. He said: Just as those who were led astray in Hell by what they used to worship in this world other than God of gods and idols, their gods and idols, God leads astray the people of disbelief in Him from Him, from His mercy and worship. He does not protect them and save them from the Fire, nor does He aid them and lighten the affliction they are in.
"Besides God. They said, 'They have gone astray from us.' Rather, we did not call upon anything before. Thus does God mislead the disbelievers."
God Almighty means by His statement,
h
That is because you used to exult upon the earth without right

, this is what We have done to you today, O people, by punishing you with the punishment you are in, because of the joy you used to rejoice in this world, because of what He permitted you to do other than it of falsehood and sins, and because of your exultation in it. Exultation is wickedness and arrogance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Because you used to exult upon the earth without right to Then evil is the abode of the arrogant

. He said: Exultation and joy mean pride and conceit, and working on the earth with sin, and that was in polytheism, and it is like His statement to Qarun, "When his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, God does not like the exultant.'" (al-Qasas 28:76). And that is in polytheism.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Because you used to exult upon the earth without right and because you used to be insolent
, he said: You acted insolently and showed off.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his statement,
h
You act in a haughty manner
, he said:
h
You act in a haughty manner

x: And His statement:
h
Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally

. God Almighty says to them: Enter the seven gates of Hell, from each gate a portion allotted to you. So evil is the abode of the arrogant. He says: So evil is the abode of those who are arrogant in this world to believe in God’s oneness and His messengers today: Hell.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “So be patient, O Muhammad, with what these polytheists argue with you about the verses of God that We sent down to you, and with their denial of you, for God will fulfill for you concerning them what He promised you of victory over them, dominance over them, and inflict punishment upon them, as was our way with Moses, son of Imran, and those who denied him. “Then either We show you some of what We promise them” God Almighty says: Then either We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime some of what We promise these polytheists of torment and punishment that will befall them, “or We take you before that befalls them. Then to Us they will be returned He says: To Us is your destiny and their destiny, and then We will judge between you and them with justice by immortally immortalizing them in the Fire, and honoring you with our neighborhood in the Gardens of Bliss.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And We have certainly sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you, to their nations, among them are those about whom We have told you their stories, and among them are those about whom We have not told you their stories.” Anas mentioned that they were eight thousand.
The narrator mentioned that:

c: Ali bin Shuaib Al-Sammar told us: Ma’n bin Isa told us: Ibrahim bin Al-Muhajir bin Mismar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Yazid bin Aban, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of whom were from the Children of Israel.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Yunus told us, on the authority of Utbah al-Basri al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Sahl, on the authority of Wahb ibn Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Sur al-Azdi, on the authority of Salman, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God sent four thousand prophets.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Hussein Al-Tirmidhi told me: Adam bin Abi Iyas told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yahya, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement,
h
Some of them We have told you about
, and some of them We have not told you about, he said: God sent an Ethiopian slave as a prophet, and he is the one We have not told you about. And His statement,
h
And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission

, meaning, “And We did not grant to any messenger from among those We sent before you, of whom We have related to you and those of whom We have not related to you, to their peoples, that he should bring to his people a sign distinguishing between him and them except by God’s permission for him to do so, so he brings it to them.” God, the Most High, says to His Prophet, “For this reason, He did not grant you the right to bring to your people what they ask of you of signs without Our permission to do so, just as We did not grant to any of Our messengers before you except that We gave them permission to do so. “So when the command of God comes, it will be judged with truth,” meaning with justice, which is that He will save His messengers and those who believed with them. And there the falsifiers will lose, meaning, there will perish those who fabricated falsehood in their false speech, their fabrications against God, and their calling upon a partner for Him.

x: God Almighty says, God to whom no deity is fit except Him, O polytheists from Quraysh, Who has made for you the grazing livestock of camels, cows, sheep, horses, and other beasts that the people of Islam keep for riding or for food that you may ride some of them meaning the donkeys and the sheep and eat of them meaning the camels, cows, and sheep. And He said, that you may ride some of them meaning that you may ride some of them and eat of them, so He omitted it because the speech indicates what was omitted.
And His saying,
h
And you have benefits in them

, is that He made for you from their hides houses that you find light on the day of your departure and the day of your stay, and from their wool, fur, and hair, furniture and provisions for a time. And His statement, And that you may accomplish through it a need in your hearts, means: And that you may accomplish through the load on some of them, and that is the camel, a need in your hearts that you would not have been able to accomplish without it, except with great difficulty, as the Most High said, And that you may carry your loads to a land which you could not have reached except with great difficulty (al-Nahl 16:7). And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: And that you may convey through it a need in your hearts means the camels that carry your loads to a country.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And that you may convey to her a need in your hearts for whatever your need was. His saying: And upon them means: And upon these camels, and similar to them of the ridden livestock. And upon the ships means: And upon the ships. You are carried. He says: We carry you upon these on land, and upon these at sea.

x: And He shows you His signs He says: And He shows you His proofs, So which of the signs of God do you deny? He says: So which of the proofs of God that He shows you, O people, in the heavens and the earth, do you deny the validity of, so you lie because of their corruption in the oneness of God, and you call upon a god other than Him.

God the Almighty says: “Have these disputants among your people, O Muhammad, not traveled to Syria and Yemen in the land? They traveled in winter and summer, so that they could see in the land they had trodden, and see what We had done to those nations before them, and see what punishment We brought upon them because of their denial of Our messengers and their rejection of Our signs. How was the end of their denial? “They were more numerous than them.” He says: Those who came before these disbelievers from Quraysh were more numerous than these, more powerful, stronger in strength, and more lasting in the land, because they used to carve houses out of the mountains and build factories.
And Mujahid used to say: Concerning this, Al-Harith narrated to me, saying:

c: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And traces on the earth means the walking with their feet. But what they used to earn availed them means: When Our punishment and might came to them, what they used to build in the mountains did not avail them, nor did that protect them from anything, but they all perished and were destroyed. It has been said that the meaning of His statement: But what availed them is: What availed them? According to this interpretation, the first ma should be in the accusative case, and the second in the nominative case. He says: So for these disputants from among your people, O Muhammad, there is a lesson in them if they pay heed, and a warning if they take heed. And when Our punishment befalls the criminal people, nothing can repel it, and nothing can prevent it. And it will befall them if they turn to believing in you.

x: God Almighty says: When the messengers whom God had sent to these nations before Quraysh came to them with clear proofs, meaning: with the clear arguments of God Almighty: They rejoiced in what they had of knowledge. He says: They rejoiced out of ignorance in what they had of knowledge and said: We will not be resurrected, and God will not punish us. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, They rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, he said: Their saying: We are more knowledgeable than them, we will not be punished, and we will not be resurrected.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: They rejoiced in what they had of knowledge with their ignorance. His statement:
h
And that which they used to ridicule overtook them

. He says: And that which they used to hasten to bring to His Messengers in mockery and ridicule overtook them from the punishment of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement:
h
And that which they used to ridicule overtook them is what their messengers brought them of the truth

x: God Almighty says: So when these nations that denied Our messengers saw Our punishment, meaning that the punishment that God promised them through His messengers had come upon them.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: So when they saw Our might, he said: the punishments that befell them. And His statement: They said, ‘We believe in God alone,’ means: They said, We have acknowledged the oneness of God, and we have believed that there is no god but God, and we have disbelieved in what we used to associate with Him, meaning: We have denied the gods that we used to associate with God before our time in our worship, and we worshipped them along with Him, and we took them as gods, so we have disavowed them.

x: God Almighty says: Their belief in the Oneness of God in this world did not benefit them when they saw that His punishment had descended and His torment had arrived, because they believed when belief does not benefit the one who believes, since God’s judgment had already passed from His knowledge, that whoever repents after the punishment from God descends for denying Him, his repentance will not benefit him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment: When they saw the punishment of God in this world, faith did not benefit them at that time. And His statement: The law of God that has already been in effect with His servants means: God, the Blessed and Exalted, did not forgive them, nor accept their repentance, nor did He make them return to faith in God and to belief in His messengers after they had witnessed His wrath. He brought down upon them His law that had already been in effect with His creation, and for that reason He did not forgive them nor accept their repentance in that situation.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatajah,
m: The law of God that has passed with His servants means: This was the law of God with those who passed before, when they saw the punishment of God, their faith would not benefit them at that time. And His statement:
h
And there the disbelievers will lose

, meaning: And he will perish when the wrath of God comes, so his deal will be lost and he will trade the Hereafter for this world, forgiveness for punishment, and faith for disbelief. The disbelievers in their Lord, the ones who deny the Oneness of their Creator, who take for themselves gods besides Him whom they worship instead of their Creator.

notes.en: This is from a rajaz poem by Abū Ḥayyān al-Faqʿasī; it is also attributed to Musāwir b. Hind al-ʿAbsī. Al-Tirmidhī and al-Baṭalyūsī affirm the latter attribution; others attribute it to al-ʿAjjāj. Al-Sīrāfī says its poet was al-Tadmurī, and al-Ṣaghānī says it was a client of Banū ʿAbs. See Sharḥ shawāhid al-Mughnī (2/973).
